title: The Doctrine of the Holy Spirit — Unit 6

blocks.en: The Spirit's Work in Salvation
blocks.es_reference: La obra del Espíritu en la salvación

blocks.en: How the Spirit applies salvation to the believer: new birth, indwelling, sealing, adoption, the baptism into one body, and the filling of the Spirit
blocks.es_reference: Lo que el Espíritu hace en quien lo recibe: el nuevo nacimiento, la morada interior, el sello, el testimonio de adopción, el bautismo en un cuerpo, y la plenitud

blocks.en: 1. What the Spirit Does in the One Who Receives Him
blocks.es_reference: 1. Lo que el Espíritu hace en quien lo recibe

blocks.en: In the last unit we saw the Spirit poured out on all flesh at Pentecost, given freely to everyone who turns to Christ. Now we ask a closer question: what does the Spirit do in the one who receives Him? The answer is breathtaking. The Spirit does not merely visit the believer or assist him from the outside; He gives new life, takes up residence within, marks the believer as God's own, assures him that he is a child of God, joins him to the body of Christ, and fills him for holy living. We will take these one at a time, for every one of them is the Spirit's work and not our own, the free gift of God to all who believe. What the Old Testament longed for and Pentecost began, the Spirit now does in every heart that trusts the Lord Jesus, and He does it not partly but fully, not for a season but forever.
blocks.es_reference: En la unidad anterior vimos al Espíritu derramado sobre toda carne en Pentecostés, dado libremente a todo aquel que se vuelve a Cristo. Ahora preguntamos algo más de cerca: ¿qué hace el Espíritu en quien lo recibe? La respuesta es asombrosa. El Espíritu no solo visita al creyente ni lo asiste desde afuera; da nueva vida, toma residencia adentro, marca al creyente como propiedad de Dios, le asegura que es hijo de Dios, lo une al cuerpo de Cristo, y lo llena para una vida santa. Tomaremos estas una por una, pues cada una de ellas es obra del Espíritu y no nuestra, el don gratuito de Dios a todos los que creen. Lo que el Antiguo Testamento anheló y Pentecostés comenzó, el Espíritu lo hace ahora en todo corazón que confía en el Señor Jesús, y lo hace no en parte sino plenamente, no por una temporada sino para siempre.

blocks.en: 2. He Gives New Birth
blocks.es_reference: 2. Da el nuevo nacimiento

blocks.en: The first and deepest work of the Spirit in salvation is the new birth. When Nicodemus came to Jesus by night, the Lord told him, "Unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit" (John 3:5-6). We do not give ourselves this birth any more than a baby gives itself its first birth; it is the Spirit who makes a dead soul alive. Paul says God "saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit" (Titus 3:5). This birth is not the work of water baptism, as though a ceremony could make a sinner new; it is the cleansing, renewing work of the Spirit Himself, granting a new heart to one who could never produce it. This is why Jesus said to Nicodemus, "You must be born again" (John 3:7), and likened the new birth to the wind that blows where it wishes (John 3:8); we feel its effect though we cannot command its working. Apart from this work no one can see the kingdom of God.
blocks.es_reference: La primera y más honda obra del Espíritu en la salvación es el nuevo nacimiento. Cuando Nicodemo vino a Jesús de noche, el Señor le dijo: “el que no naciere de agua y del Espíritu, no puede entrar en el reino de Dios. Lo que es nacido de la carne, carne es; y lo que es nacido del Espíritu, espíritu es” (Juan 3:5-6). No nos damos este nacimiento más de lo que un bebé se da a sí mismo su primer nacimiento; es el Espíritu quien hace viva un alma muerta. Pablo dice que Dios “nos salvó, por el lavamiento de la regeneración y la renovación del Espíritu Santo” (Tito 3:5). Este nacimiento no es la obra del bautismo en agua, como si una ceremonia pudiera hacer nuevo a un pecador; es la obra limpiadora y renovadora del Espíritu mismo, dando un nuevo corazón a quien jamás podría producirlo. Por eso Jesús dijo a Nicodemo: “Os es necesario nacer de nuevo” (Juan 3:7), y comparó el nuevo nacimiento con el viento que sopla de donde quiere (Juan 3:8); sentimos su efecto aunque no podamos mandar su obrar. Aparte de esta obra nadie puede ver el reino de Dios.

blocks.en: 3. He Comes to Dwell Within
blocks.es_reference: 3. Viene a morar adentro

blocks.en: The same Spirit who gives the new birth then comes to live within the one He has made alive. This is the very thing Ezekiel had promised, that God would put His Spirit within His people. Now it is fulfilled in every believer. Paul writes plainly, "if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not His" (Romans 8:9). The indwelling Spirit is not the privilege of a few advanced Christians; He is the mark of belonging to Christ at all. Your body, says Paul, "is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God" (1 Corinthians 6:19). The God of heaven has come to live inside ordinary believers. This is why the Christian life is not a matter of trying harder in our own strength, but of yielding to the One who already dwells within. Every believer, the weakest and the strongest alike, is a dwelling place of God by His Spirit.
blocks.es_reference: El mismo Espíritu que da el nuevo nacimiento viene luego a vivir dentro de aquel a quien ha hecho vivo. Esto es lo mismo que Ezequiel había prometido, que Dios pondría su Espíritu dentro de su pueblo. Ahora se cumple en todo creyente. Pablo escribe claramente: “si alguno no tiene el Espíritu de Cristo, el tal no es de él” (Romanos 8:9). La morada del Espíritu no es el privilegio de unos pocos cristianos avanzados; es la marca misma de pertenecer a Cristo. Vuestro cuerpo, dice Pablo, “es templo del Espíritu Santo, el cual está en vosotros, el cual tenéis de Dios” (1 Corintios 6:19). El Dios del cielo ha venido a vivir dentro de creyentes comunes. Por eso la vida cristiana no es cuestión de esforzarnos más en nuestra propia fuerza, sino de entregarnos a Aquel que ya mora adentro. Todo creyente, el más débil y el más fuerte por igual, es morada de Dios por su Espíritu.

blocks.en: 4. He Seals Us as God's Own
blocks.es_reference: 4. Nos sella como propiedad de Dios

blocks.en: The Spirit also seals the believer. Paul says that in Christ, "having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise, who is the guarantee of our inheritance" (Ephesians 1:13-14). In the ancient world a king pressed his signet ring into soft wax upon an important document, and that seal marked the paper as his own, under his authority and protection. So the Spirit Himself is God's mark upon the believer, declaring that we belong to Him. This is why Paul could call Him the One "by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption" (Ephesians 4:30). The seal is also a down payment, a guarantee that the full inheritance is surely coming. The Spirit we now possess is God's pledge that He will finish what He has begun and bring us safely home. A seal in those days meant two things at once, ownership and security: the document so marked belonged to the king and was safe under his authority. So the Spirit declares both that we are God's and that we are kept by God, until the day He claims His own.
blocks.es_reference: El Espíritu también sella al creyente. Pablo dice que en Cristo, “habiendo creído, fuisteis sellados con el Espíritu Santo de la promesa, que es las arras de nuestra herencia” (Efesios 1:13-14). En el mundo antiguo un rey imprimía su anillo de sello en la cera blanda sobre un documento importante, y aquel sello marcaba el papel como suyo, bajo su autoridad y protección. Así el Espíritu mismo es la marca de Dios sobre el creyente, declarando que le pertenecemos. Por eso Pablo pudo llamarlo Aquel “con el cual estáis sellados para el día de la redención” (Efesios 4:30). El sello es también un pago inicial, una garantía de que la herencia plena ciertamente viene. El Espíritu que ahora poseemos es la prenda de Dios de que terminará lo que ha comenzado y nos llevará a salvo a casa. Un sello en aquellos días significaba dos cosas a la vez, propiedad y seguridad: el documento así marcado pertenecía al rey y estaba seguro bajo su autoridad. Así el Espíritu declara a la vez que somos de Dios y que somos guardados por Dios, hasta el día en que reclame lo suyo.

blocks.en: 5. He Assures Us We Are God's Children
blocks.es_reference: 5. Nos asegura que somos hijos de Dios

blocks.en: The indwelling Spirit also brings the believer assurance. We do not have to wonder whether God has received us, for the Spirit Himself testifies that He has. Paul writes, "you received the Spirit of adoption by whom we cry out, 'Abba, Father.' The Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God" (Romans 8:15-16). It is the Spirit who teaches a frightened sinner to call the holy God his Father. The word Abba is the tender, familiar name a child uses for his own father, and it is the Spirit who puts that word in our mouths, assuring the doubting heart that it truly belongs to God. This witness is one of the sweetest of His works, for it turns slaves into sons and fear into the confidence of a child who knows he is loved.
blocks.es_reference: El Espíritu que mora adentro trae también seguridad al creyente. No tenemos que preguntarnos si Dios nos ha recibido, pues el Espíritu mismo testifica que sí. Pablo escribe: “recibisteis el espíritu de adopción, por el cual clamamos: Abba, Padre. El Espíritu mismo da testimonio a nuestro espíritu, de que somos hijos de Dios” (Romanos 8:15-16). Es el Espíritu quien enseña a un pecador atemorizado a llamar Padre al Dios santo. La palabra Abba es el nombre tierno y familiar que un niño usa para su propio padre, y es el Espíritu quien pone esa palabra en nuestra boca, asegurando al corazón dudoso que de veras pertenece a Dios. Este testimonio es una de las más dulces de sus obras, pues vuelve a los esclavos en hijos y al temor en la confianza de un niño que sabe que es amado.

blocks.en: 6. Baptized with the Spirit into One Body
blocks.es_reference: 6. Bautizados en el Espíritu en un cuerpo

blocks.en: Jesus had promised that His disciples would be baptized with the Holy Spirit, and on the day of Pentecost it came to pass. But this baptism is not the privilege of a special class of believers; it is true of every Christian. Paul says, "by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body... and have all been made to drink into one Spirit" (1 Corinthians 12:13). To be baptized with the Spirit is to be placed, at conversion, into the body of Christ, joined to the Lord and to all His people. Notice the word all: not some, but all who belong to Christ have been baptized by the one Spirit into the one body. This is a settled fact accomplished when we are saved, not a later experience reserved for a favored few. We need not seek some second blessing to make us fully Christ's, for if we are His at all, the one Spirit has already baptized us into His one body.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús había prometido que sus discípulos serían bautizados con el Espíritu Santo, y en el día de Pentecostés se cumplió. Pero este bautismo no es el privilegio de una clase especial de creyentes; es verdad de todo cristiano. Pablo dice: “por un solo Espíritu somos todos bautizados en un cuerpo... y a todos se nos dio a beber de un mismo Espíritu” (1 Corintios 12:13). Ser bautizado con el Espíritu es ser puesto, en la conversión, en el cuerpo de Cristo, unido al Señor y a todo su pueblo. Note la palabra todos: no algunos, sino todos los que pertenecen a Cristo han sido bautizados por el un Espíritu en el un cuerpo. Esto es un hecho establecido, cumplido cuando somos salvos, no una experiencia posterior reservada a unos pocos favorecidos. No necesitamos buscar alguna segunda bendición para ser plenamente de Cristo, pues si somos suyos en absoluto, el un Espíritu ya nos ha bautizado en su un cuerpo.

blocks.en: 7. Be Filled with the Spirit
blocks.es_reference: 7. Sed llenos del Espíritu

blocks.en: If the baptism with the Spirit happens once, the filling of the Spirit is meant to happen again and again. Paul commands, "do not be drunk with wine, in which is dissipation; but be filled with the Spirit" (Ephesians 5:18). It is a striking comparison. A man controlled by strong drink is ruled by it; his words and steps are no longer his own. The believer is to be that fully under the Spirit's control, not by wine but by surrender to God. The likeness runs all through Scripture: when Hannah prayed in deep earnestness, Eli thought she was drunk (1 Samuel 1:13-14), and when the Spirit fell at Pentecost the crowd said the believers were full of new wine (Acts 2:13-15). The Spirit-filled life can look like that to the watching world, overflowing and unashamed, glad in God beyond what mere wine could ever give. And we may be filled again and again, as the early disciples were, for those who had been filled at Pentecost were filled afresh when they prayed (Acts 4:31). Paul describes what the filled life looks like: it speaks and sings to the Lord, it gives thanks always, and it serves others in humility (Ephesians 5:19-21). To be filled is to be repeatedly yielded to the Spirit, letting Him fill what we daily empty before Him, so that He may govern our speech, our worship, and our walk.
blocks.es_reference: Si el bautismo con el Espíritu sucede una vez, la plenitud del Espíritu ha de suceder una y otra vez. Pablo manda: “no os embriaguéis con vino, en lo cual hay disolución; antes bien sed llenos del Espíritu” (Efesios 5:18). Es una comparación llamativa. Un hombre dominado por la bebida fuerte es gobernado por ella; sus palabras y sus pasos ya no son suyos. El creyente ha de estar así de plenamente bajo el control del Espíritu, no por el vino sino por la entrega a Dios. La semejanza corre por toda la Escritura: cuando Ana oraba con hondo fervor, Elí la tuvo por borracha (1 Samuel 1:13-14), y cuando el Espíritu cayó en Pentecostés la multitud dijo que los creyentes estaban llenos de mosto (Hechos 2:13-15). La vida llena del Espíritu puede parecerle eso al mundo que observa, rebosante y sin vergüenza, alegre en Dios más de lo que el vino podría jamás dar. Y podemos ser llenos una y otra vez, como lo fueron los primeros discípulos, pues los que habían sido llenos en Pentecostés fueron llenos de nuevo cuando oraron (Hechos 4:31). Pablo describe cómo es la vida llena: habla y canta al Señor, da gracias siempre, y sirve a los demás con humildad (Efesios 5:19-21). Ser llenos es estar repetidamente entregados al Espíritu, dejándole llenar lo que diariamente vaciamos ante Él, para que gobierne nuestra habla, nuestra adoración, y nuestro andar.

blocks.en: 8. The Question of Tongues and the Gifts Today
blocks.es_reference: 8. La cuestión de las lenguas y los dones hoy

blocks.en: Wherever the Spirit's work is discussed, the question of tongues and the miraculous gifts arises, and we ought to speak of it plainly and with charity. At Pentecost the believers spoke in real languages, so that the gathered nations heard the gospel each in his own tongue. Paul wrote much about such gifts in his letters to Corinth, and there he laid down truths that should guide us. The gifts are distributed by the Spirit as He wills, and they are not the same for everyone; when Paul asks, "Do all speak with tongues?" (1 Corinthians 12:30), he plainly expects the answer to be no. He sets love above every gift, and he insists that whatever is done be done for the building up of the church and in good order. Sincere Christians differ on whether the sign-gifts continue today as they did at the first, or whether they served the founding age of the church and the completing of Scripture. Some hold that these gifts served to found the church and to confirm the apostles' message while the Scriptures were still being written, and so passed away when that work was complete; others believe they continue to this day. On this our churches must extend charity to one another and not divide over what Scripture does not make a test of fellowship. But all may agree on the tests the Spirit Himself gives: whatever is truly of the Spirit will exalt Christ as Lord, will accord with the Scriptures, and will be governed by love. We will look more closely at the gifts of the Spirit, and at love as the greatest of them all, near the end of this course.
blocks.es_reference: Dondequiera que se trata la obra del Espíritu surge la cuestión de las lenguas y los dones milagrosos, y debemos hablar de ella con claridad y con caridad. En Pentecostés los creyentes hablaron en lenguas reales, de modo que las naciones reunidas oyeron el evangelio cada una en su propio idioma. Pablo escribió mucho sobre tales dones en sus cartas a Corinto, y allí estableció verdades que deben guiarnos. Los dones son repartidos por el Espíritu como Él quiere, y no son los mismos para todos; cuando Pablo pregunta: “¿Hablan todos lenguas?” (1 Corintios 12:30), claramente espera que la respuesta sea no. Pone el amor por encima de todo don, e insiste en que cuanto se haga, se haga para edificación de la iglesia y con buen orden. Cristianos sinceros difieren en si los dones de señales continúan hoy como al principio, o si sirvieron a la edad fundadora de la iglesia y a completar la Escritura. Algunos sostienen que estos dones sirvieron para fundar la iglesia y confirmar el mensaje de los apóstoles mientras las Escrituras aún se escribían, y así pasaron cuando esa obra se completó; otros creen que continúan hasta hoy. En esto nuestras iglesias deben extender caridad unas a otras y no dividirse sobre lo que la Escritura no hace prueba de comunión. Pero todos pueden concordar en las pruebas que el Espíritu mismo da: cuanto es de veras del Espíritu exaltará a Cristo como Señor, concordará con las Escrituras, y será gobernado por el amor. Veremos más de cerca los dones del Espíritu, y el amor como el mayor de todos, cerca del fin de este curso.

The indwelling of the Spirit fulfills what the prophet ____ had promised, that God would put His Spirit within His people.
Paul says the believer's body "is the ____ of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God" (1 Corinthians 6:19).
Believers were "sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise, who is the ____ of our inheritance" (Ephesians 1:13-14).
A seal in the ancient world meant two things at once: ownership and ____.

sa.prompt: What does the Holy Spirit do in giving the new birth?
sa.model: The Spirit gives new life, so that a person is born again, born of the Spirit, as Jesus told Nicodemus. Paul calls it the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Spirit. The new birth is the Spirit's work, not something we produce by our own decision or good works.

sa.prompt: What does Romans 8:9 teach about the indwelling of the Spirit?
sa.model: It teaches that the Spirit of God dwells in the believer, and that if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not His. So the indwelling Spirit marks everyone who truly belongs to Christ, and in the new covenant this indwelling is permanent, abiding forever.

sa.prompt: What does it mean that believers are sealed with the Spirit?
sa.model: It means God has marked us as His own with the Holy Spirit, as a king marked his papers with a signet ring. The Spirit is the guarantee of our inheritance, sealing us for the day of redemption, which shows the believer's security and certain belonging to God.

sa.prompt: How does the Spirit assure us that we are God's children?
sa.model: The Spirit of adoption causes us to cry out, Abba, Father, and the Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God. So our assurance of being God's children is the Spirit's own inward witness, not merely our feelings.

sa.prompt: Explain the baptism with the Spirit into one body.
sa.model: Paul says that by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body. This baptism happens once, joining every believer to the body of Christ at salvation. It is not a repeated experience for a chosen few but the common possession of all who belong to Christ.

sa.prompt: What does “be filled with the Spirit” mean, and how does it differ from the baptism with the Spirit?
sa.model: To be filled with the Spirit, commanded in Ephesians 5:18, is to be repeatedly yielded to His control, and it is meant to happen again and again. The baptism with the Spirit happens once and joins us to the body; the filling is the ongoing surrender by which the Spirit governs our life.

sa.prompt: Explain the comparison between drunkenness and being filled with the Spirit.
sa.model: As a man controlled by strong drink is ruled by it, so the believer is to be fully under the Spirit's control, not by wine but by surrender to God. The likeness runs through Scripture: Eli thought Hannah was drunk, and the Pentecost crowd thought the believers were drunk; the filled life overflows with gladness in God.

sa.prompt: How does this unit handle the question of whether the sign-gifts continue today?
sa.model: It speaks plainly and with charity, noting that sincere Christians differ. Some hold the sign-gifts served to found the church and confirm the message while Scripture was being written, and so passed away; others believe they continue. The unit urges charity and not dividing over what Scripture does not make a test of fellowship.

sa.prompt: What tests does the Spirit Himself give for discerning His genuine work?
sa.model: Whatever is truly of the Spirit will exalt Christ as Lord, will accord with the Scriptures, and will be governed by love. These tests hold whatever one concludes about the gifts, for the Spirit's work always points to Christ and never contradicts the Word.

sa.prompt: Summarize the Spirit's work in the believer's salvation.
sa.model: The Spirit gives the new birth, comes to dwell within permanently, seals us as God's own, and assures us we are His children, crying Abba, Father. He baptizes every believer into one body and fills those who yield to Him. The whole work is God's gift, not something we earn.
